entities.summary: Hélias de Saint-Yrieix was a French Benedictine abbot, papal judiciary official, bishop, and Cardinal. He served as papal legate in Avignon from 1343 to 1344 and played a key role in the French papal court. De Saint-Yrieix was instrumental in the Avignon Papacy's relations with the Kingdom of France and the Holy Roman Empire. He was a prominent figure in the papal judiciary, overseeing the administration of justice for the papacy. De Saint-Yrieix's tenure as papal legate was marked by significant events, including the Avignon Papal Schism and the Treaty of Corbeil. His legacy extends to the French monarchy, where he influenced the development of papal policy. De Saint-Yrieix's contributions to the papal court and his role in shaping French politics have left a lasting impact on the region. His story is a testament to the complex web of power and influence that defined the medieval period. The intricate dance of church and state, with its shifting alliances and power struggles, was a hallmark of the era. Hélias de Saint-Yrieix's place in this narrative is one of significance, as his actions and decisions had far-reaching consequences for the region. His story serves as a reminder of the power of human agency and the complex interplay of historical forces that shape our world.

entities.summary:
Hélias de Saint-Yrieix was a French Benedictine abbot, papal judiciary official, bishop and Cardinal who played a pivotal role in shaping Western Europe's ecclesiastical politics during the 14th century.

As papal legate to France from 1337 until his death in 1367, Hélias de Saint-Yrieix worked closely with King Philip VI to implement reforms within the French Catholic Church. His efforts contributed significantly to the development of a more centralized and bureaucratic church structure.

De Saint-Yrieix's influence extended beyond ecclesiastical politics, as he was also a key figure in the diplomatic relations between France and the Holy Roman Empire during this period. He played a crucial role in resolving several border disputes between the two powers, which helped maintain peace in Western Europe for several decades.

De Saint-Yrieix's legacy can be seen in the continued development of papal authority within the Catholic Church, as well as his impact on French politics and diplomacy during the 14th century. His contributions to these fields have had a lasting impact on the course of Western European history.

In the world of art, de Saint-Yrieix's name is still remembered today for his patronage of several notable artists and architects of the time, including the famous French architect Pierre de Chelles.
